result:
Understood, I'll write it up. One thing comes first, and it's quick: we've settled *what* it does but not *how* it gets built. Here are the three real options, with my pick.

**A. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** New pages and tables in the existing Flask app, in the same SQLite database on the office Pi. The brewing side lives in its own section of the code, so it doesn't tangle with tabs.
- Gains: nothing new to install, run, or back up. The scanner and label printer hook into the app you already have.
- Costs: brewing and the taproom share one Pi. If it goes down, both are down.

**B. A separate small app on the same Pi.** Same tools as A, but its own program and its own database.
- Gains: a problem on the brewing side can't touch tabs, and the other way round.
- Costs: a second service to keep running and a second database to back up.

**C. Off-the-shelf brewery software** (there are hosted products that do lot tracing).
- Gains: little to build.
- Costs: a monthly fee, your data on someone else's servers, and no guarantee it works with your scanner and label printer.

I'd go with A. It's the least to run, and keeping the code in its own section gives most of B's separation.

Whichever we pick, the Pi's SD card becomes the only record linking each bottle to its sacks. The design will include a regular off-box backup.

This is project-sized. I'll write a full design document, and a reviewer will read it before you do. I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer.

Unless you'd rather go with B or C, I'll go with A and send the design next.
